Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling policy

Source: R/policies-etc-ucb-thompson.R
policy_thompson.Rd

Maintains an independent Beta posterior for each arm's success probability, draws one sample from every posterior at each step and selects the arm with the largest draw. Rewards must be 0 or 1; the update adds the reward to the arm's alpha and 1 - reward to its beta.

Usage

policy_thompson(alpha = 1, beta = 1)

Arguments

alpha, beta

Positive prior shape parameters, recycled across arms. The default Beta(1, 1) prior is uniform.

Value

A bandit_policy object.

Details

The logged propensity is NA: the marginal selection probability of Thompson sampling is the posterior probability that the arm's draw is the maximum, which has no simple closed form. Logging NA is honest; estimating it by simulation is possible but consumes additional random numbers and is not done here.

References

Thompson, W. R. (1933). On the likelihood that one unknown probability exceeds another in view of the evidence of two samples. Biometrika 25(3-4), 285-294. doi:10.2307/2332286

Russo, D. J., Van Roy, B., Kazerouni, A., Osband, I., Wen, Z. (2018). A tutorial on Thompson sampling. Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 11(1), 1-96. doi:10.1561/2200000070

See also

policy_ucb1(), run_experiment()

Examples

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(a = 0.2, b = 0.5))
run_experiment(env, policy_thompson(), horizon = 500, seed = 1)
#> <bandit_result> 1 policy x 1 replicate x horizon 500 (seed 1)
#> environment: bernoulli_environment (2 arms)
#> stored: summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   policy          replications mean_regret median_regret regret_q025 regret_q975
#> * <chr>                  <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 thompson_policy            1         7.8           7.8         7.8         7.8
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_reward <dbl>, mean_optimal_share <dbl>
